Littleton non-profits ranked by government grant revenue in 2024
Y. J. Macias
Colorado Agency For Recovery Residences led non-profits in Littleton, Colorado in reported government grant revenue in 2024, with $1,153,388 in government grants reported in its IRS Form 990 filing and $1,287,292 in total revenue. Government grants made up 89.6% of its reported total revenue.
The ranking reflects non-profits with available Form 990-series government grant revenue data that met the ranking's data criteria and may not include every non-profit in the city.
The ranking is based on IRS Form 990 filings, the annual information returns most tax-exempt organizations file with the IRS. The form includes reported revenue, expenses, assets, governance information and compensation paid to certain people, making it a public source for comparing large tax-exempt organizations' finances.
The figures reflect what each organization reported for its filing year, including total revenue, contributions, government grants, compensation, the number of employees and assets at the start and end of the year. Because nonprofits can differ by mission, structure and accounting period, the totals are best read as reported financial measures, not as a direct measure of local charitable activity.
Among the 10 ranked organizations with calculable government-grant shares, the median government-grant share was 10.2%. The organization with the highest government-grant share was Colorado Agency For Recovery Residences at 89.6%.
Colorado Agency For Recovery Residences reported $1,153,388 in government grant revenue in 2024, up from $410,595 the prior year—a reported increase of $742,793 or 180.9%.
Several organizations provided additional financial context for the year. For example, The Colorado Center For The Blind received $7,659,147 in total contributions, of which $7,440,467 was categorized as all other contributions. Non-cash contributions amounted to $7,061,339. National Federation Of The Blind Of Colorado reported $441,984 in total contributions, with $242,719 as all other contributions and $3,500 reported as non-cash.
Asset balances also shifted among ranked organizations. Colorado Agency For Recovery Residences reported end-of-year assets of $420,723, up from a beginning balance of $295,053 (a 42.6% increase). The Colorado Center For The Blind saw its assets increase from $3,910,403 to $11,075,756, a rise of 183.2%.
Tax-exempt organizations include a wide range of groups, such as charities, foundations, educational institutions and other mission-driven organizations. Under IRS rules, 501(c)(3) organizations must be organized and operated for exempt purposes, and their earnings cannot benefit private shareholders or individuals.
